title: Target anatomy
view: Right side of the head, seen from the right: head up, face to the right. Same view and scale as the positioning image. Skin see-through over the superficial nerves.
teachingPoint: The auricle is supplied from three directions by superficial nerves that all cross a subcutaneous ring round its base; the concha is supplied deep (vagus) and is not covered by the ring.
claims: Standard adult anatomy, not from the record: auriculotemporal nerve rising just in front of the tragus, behind the superficial temporal artery; great auricular nerve rising from below toward the lobe, with anterior and posterior branches; lesser occipital nerve rising behind the ear with a twig to the upper back of the auricle.
Teal: the ring of subcutaneous anaesthetic through the two puncture sites (record, steps 2-6). Each of the three nerves crosses it.
Purple dashed zone: the concha, supplied by the vagus/facial nerves deeper inside and not blocked by the ring (record, troubleshooting).
Four labels: Auriculotemporal n., Great auricular n., Lesser occipital n., Concha.

geometry.why: auriculotemporal nerve runs in front of the tragus
the nerve lies behind the superficial temporal artery
auriculotemporal trunk stays off the auricle
great auricular nerve comes from below the lobe
lesser occipital nerve runs behind the ear
concha zone is inside the auricle
